_comment: Findings-report corpora. The report generator knows nothing about any
particular comparison; a corpus profile tells it which repos the findings
cite, where the captured evidence lives, and how to turn a path as written
in a finding into a path inside a repo. Adding a corpus is a data edit,
A run picks its corpus from, in order: an explicit --corpus flag, the
backlog's top-level "corpus" field, .corpus-meta.json, then the default
below. See tim/src/parity/corpus-profile.js, which copies the precedence
sides[] is a list, not a pair. The requirements side will not always be a
prototype and there will not always be two of them; nothing here assumes
the number two. repos{} is keyed by repo, not by side, because a finding
on the frontend side routinely cites the backend.
pathRoots is ordered longest-first and each entry strips its prefix to
leave a repo-relative path. The bare prefixes come last because they are
prefixes of nothing else; impliedPrefix re-normalises a path that was
already repo-relative when it was written.
This file lives in tools/ rather than tim/src/ because the shell entry
points in this directory read it too.

dr21.description: The real live-animals frontend against Design release 2.1 of the GB notification service prototype. 97 findings, captured August 2026.
_pinComment: Which commit each repo's citations resolve against. Sam ruled on 18 Aug
2026 to photograph the latest of both sides rather than the corpus
commits (32f6106c frontend, 7da4f70 prototype), so every pin is HEAD and
a finding written against the older markup is re-verified rather than
re-pinned. backend and address-book were never pinned by the corpus at
all; they are pinned here so their citations resolve at all.

frontend.why: Sam's ruling: latest of both sides, not the corpus commit 32f6106c.

prototype.why: Sam's ruling: re-pin off 7da4f70 to the prototype head, so the 15 findings the address-book push moved are corrected automatically rather than by hand.

backend.why: Never pinned by the corpus. Pinned here so the 21 backend-gated findings' citations resolve; treat it as a verification pin, not a comparison pin.

address-book.why: Never pinned by the corpus. Same as backend.

_captureComment: What the pictures on disk are actually of. A pin is where the citations
point; a capture is where the pixels came from. They diverge the moment
a repo moves, and the report says so rather than presenting an old

prototype.note: 70 full-page shots at 1x, taken before the address-book push. Superseded once capture re-runs at the pin.

frontend.note: 34 page models mined from traces. No screenshots exist on this side; every frontend column falls back to a page-model plate.
